asks: Did you wash your hands? It is not a rule. It is only usual.
Do you know whose place this was?
Would you take the salt, or leave it for whoever is after you?
description: A slab of pale stone stands where the table was, laid with a folded cloth, a shallow dish, and a small heap of salt. Everything on it is in the only place it could be.
emotes: The dish on {it} rings once, faintly, though nothing has touched it.
The cloth on {it} lifts at one corner and lies back down.
{it} takes the light off the room and gives it back warmer.
A grain of salt slides down the cone on {it} and stops.
looks: The fold in the cloth has been like that since before the stone. Nobody folded it this morning.
The dish holds a finger of dark liquid that has not evaporated and is not going to.
The salt is heaped in a low cone with a single fingermark taken out of the side of it.
name: a stone altar, laid
says: Sit. It has been ready a long time.
It is not a shrine. It is only that everything is where it should be.
Nothing is required of you. That is what the salt is for.
